payload.headline: QQQ slips back; trend, fear and breadth still argue for standing aside

summary.thesis: Both SPY and QQQ are in downtrends. They sit below their 50- and 200-day averages and well under their Oct 28 one-month highs. Fear is 'elevated' and only 10% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. Tech is the weaker of the two.
summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term buying and swing trades. All three readings still point the same way.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 682.42 (its 200-day average and the market gate) ends the tech downtrend. A QQQ close below 608.45 or an SPY close below 689.81 would set new one-month lows, meaning the decline would be continuing.

payload.happening: SPY closed at 718.78, down 0.49% on the day from 722.29. It is down 1.86% over 5 days and 6.61% over 20 days. QQQ fell harder. It closed at 638.1, down 1.99% from 651.03, and is down 2.87% over 5 days and 11.53% over 20 days. Both peaked for the month on Oct 28: SPY at 772.31 and QQQ at 725.61. Both bottomed on Nov 20: SPY at 689.81 and QQQ at 608.45. The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. No news was recorded since the last note. Two releases are due Nov 25 at 08:30. One is the second estimate of Q3 2026 GDP and corporate profits. The other is October Personal Income and Outlays, which includes PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation measure. The jobs report follows on Dec 4.
payload.business: Trend: both indices are below their 50- and 200-day averages, so the trend is down. SPY is 1.6% below its 200-day average of 730.62. QQQ is further away, 6.9% below its 682.42. That means the selling is concentrated in tech. Fear: the VIX is labeled 'elevated', which is the 20–30 band. That is down from 'high' in the prior session, but it still ranks in the 96th percentile of the past 252 days. That reading is as of Nov 23, because the Nov 24 VIX isn't stored yet. Together: the trend is down, fear is easing but still elevated, and participation is thin. That combination describes a market still under pressure, not one that has turned.

worth.text: This note makes no valuation call. The levels are price-trend markers only.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Fear has stepped down from 'high' to 'elevated', and breadth rose to 10% from 3% in the previous note.
Both indices are holding above their Nov 20 one-month lows: SPY by 4.0% and QQQ by 4.6%.
SPY is only 1.6% below its 200-day average of 730.62, so the broad market's long-term trend line is within reach.
bear: QQQ gave back 1.99% today and is 11.0% below its 50-day average of 708.42. Tech is leading the decline.
Only 10% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so the weakness is widespread.
QQQ is down 11.53% over 20 days, and the market gate stays active until QQQ closes above 682.42.

levels.what: QQQ 200-day average and the market gate. A close above it ends the tech downtrend and would support moving to a selective stance.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
QQQ 50-day average. A close above it would put tech's short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's 'QQQ above its 50-day average' check.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 20). A close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline would be continuing.
SPY 200-day average. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
SPY 50-day average. A close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 28). A close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.

longterm.why: QQQ closed at 638.1, 6.9% below its 200-day gate of 682.42. Fear is 'elevated' as of Nov 23, and breadth is 10%. Trend, fear and breadth all still argue against new buying until QQQ closes above 682.42.

swing.why: QQQ is 11.0% below its 50-day average of 708.42. Below that level, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check, and today's 1.99% drop moved it further away.

decision.timing: Two releases are due Nov 25 at 08:30: the second estimate of Q3 GDP and corporate profits, and October Personal Income and Outlays (including PCE). The jobs report is due Dec 4 at 08:30. The fear reading is from Nov 23 because the Nov 24 VIX isn't stored yet. The nearest levels to watch are SPY 730.62 above and 689.81 below, and QQQ 682.42 above and 608.45 below.

change_mind: Toward buying: a QQQ close above 682.42 ends the tech downtrend and clears the market gate. A further close above 708.42 would put tech's short-term trend back up. An SPY close above 730.62 would restore the broad market's long-term uptrend. Rising breadth and the VIX moving down out of 'elevated' would strengthen the case.

Toward more caution: a QQQ close below 608.45 or an SPY close below 689.81 would set new one-month lows, meaning the decline would be continuing. Fear moving back into the 'high' band would also count against buying.
payload.what_changed: The previous note (Nov 23) covered a sharp rebound. Today QQQ gave back 1.99%, to 638.1 from 651.03, and SPY slipped 0.49%, to 718.78 from 722.29. Fear eased from 'high' (Nov 20 reading) to 'elevated' (Nov 23 reading), and breadth improved to 10% from 3%. The moving averages shifted slightly. QQQ's 200-day is now 682.42 (was 682.29) and its 50-day 708.42 (was 709.73). SPY's 200-day is 730.62 (was 730.47) and its 50-day 758.56 (was 759.3). The decision is unchanged: stand aside. This is research, not advice.
